text:
Stock price for Marathon Petroleum edged up 0.66% today to close at $393.52, recovering modestly from a sharp three-day sell-off that wiped out 8.5% of the stock's value between September 18 and September 23. The rebound aligns with a slight stabilization in crude oil prices after escalating geopolitical tensions between the U.S. and Iran—a refiner's fortunes hinge heavily on the spread between crude oil input costs and refined product prices (gasoline, diesel), so the uncertainty and volatility in the crude markets over the past week created real pressure on the stock.

The broader headwind remains the wide gap between U.S. crude at $96.41 and world crude at $114.89 per barrel, which constrains refining margins. Refineries are running at 94% capacity, and storage levels for gasoline and diesel are elevated, both of which suggest demand is tepid relative to supply—exactly the environment where a refiner struggles to convert cheap feedstock into profitable sales.
